articles.title: 👂 Apple's New AirPods Reportedly Have Cameras; Your Earbuds Can Now See What You See, Which Is Mostly The Floor
articles.dateline: CUPERTINO — reported into, and apparently at, my ear
paras: Rumors point to Apple building camera-equipped AirPods — AI-powered earbuds that can see what you see, finally answering the question absolutely nobody asked: "what if my headphones had eyes?"

"They understand your surroundings," sources say, of tiny devices now capable of watching your entire life from the side of your head — mostly documenting the inside of your pocket and the occasional dramatic close-up of your own shoulder. Privacy advocates have questions; the AirPods, for once, are already looking into it.

articles.title: 🧒 One A.I. Firm Builds A 'Teen' Version As Another Faces A 29-State Trial; The Industry Discovers Children Exist
paras: One AI giant announced a dedicated ChatGPT experience for teenagers just as another headed into a landmark 29-state trial over alleged harm to young users — a study in contrasts best summarized as "building the safety rail" and "explaining to a judge why there wasn't one."

"We take youth safety extremely seriously," both companies said — one while launching a feature, the other while consulting a very large legal team. Observers note the tech industry has reached the stage of maturity where it remembers, usually via subpoena, that some of its billions of users are twelve.

articles.title: 🔁 A.I. Now Designs The Chips That Run A.I.; Startup Worth $21 Billion For Closing The Loop
articles.dateline: SILICON VALLEY — reported from inside its own feedback loop
paras: AI is now compressing the time it takes to design the very chips that power AI, as a chip startup surged to a $21 billion valuation — meaning the machines are officially helping build their own brains, which is fine, which is completely fine.

"It accelerates everything," an engineer said, of a process where AI designs a faster chip that trains a smarter AI that designs a faster chip, forever, until someone finally remembers to ask where exactly this is heading. Investors, thrilled, valued the loop at $21 billion and politely declined to look directly at it.

articles.title: 🛡️ Experts Warn Everyone To Brace For A.I.-Powered Cyberattacks; The Robots Have Learned To Pick Locks At Scale
articles.dateline: THE SECURITY DESK — reported behind three firewalls
paras: Security experts are urging companies to prepare for a coming wave of AI-powered cyberattacks — automated, tireless, and clever enough to try ten thousand doors while a human is still looking for the coffee.

"The threat is evolving," specialists warned, of attackers who no longer sleep, unionize, or make typos. The recommended defense is, reassuringly, more AI — meaning the future of cybersecurity is two artificial intelligences fighting in a basement while everyone else quietly upgrades their password from 'password' to 'password1.'

articles.title: 🇬🇧 U.K. Wonders What Happens If Another Country Turns Off Its A.I.; Discovers The Cloud Has A Landlord
articles.dateline: LONDON — reported with a stiff upper lip and no internet
paras: The UK is publicly asking what happens to an economy if another country can simply cut off access to the AI models it increasingly depends on — the geopolitical version of realizing your entire life runs on a subscription someone else can cancel at will.

"We must ensure resilience," officials said, having noticed a touch late that "the cloud" is, in fact, a collection of very physical buildings in someone else's backyard. Analysts note nations are now discovering what every app user already knew: depending entirely on a service you don't control is delightful, right up until the day it isn't.

horoscopes.text: Your earbuds are watching now. Smile. Or don't. They will have a strong opinion about it either way.
Two A.I.s will fight over your security today. You may contribute by choosing a slightly longer password.
Mercury depends entirely on a cloud in another country. Feel the vulnerability. Subscribe anyway. You always do.

tech_tip: If a gadget can 'see what you see,' remember it also sees everything you'd rather it didn't. Blink twice. It's watching.
gadget_watch: Apple may put cameras in your AirPods, so your headphones now have a better view of your life than you do. Meanwhile, brace for AI-powered cyberattacks — a great week to finally retire the password 'password.'
